milestones.name: Parallel smoke solver loops with pinned reference hashes
milestones.validation: Per-cell loops (advection, boundary conditions, forces, pressure operator, vector updates, gradient subtraction, divergence check, field validation, source injection) run on rayon with every element written by the same expression as before; reductions stay serial and in index order. Final-state hashes of reference scenarios recorded before the change still match, and are equal on 1, 2 and 8 rayon threads. The pressure operator reads a precomputed open-face mask, two reductions share one pass, the step copies only the evolving fields (density, temperature, velocity), and trilinear sampling has an exact in-range path compared bit for bit with the original on about 240,000 points. A failed step leaves the committed state and clock untouched: injected failures in the collider stage, field validation and the pressure solve, then a corrected retry equals a fresh replay. Advection at 128^3 on one thread, impact scene: 1650-1770 ms before the sampling change, 1423 ms after (measured under load).
milestones.limits: Timings were measured on a loaded machine and only on x86_64 Linux, not certified. The reference hashes hold only on that platform. The Jacobi mode keeps serial in-order reductions, so its pressure solve does not scale with threads like the other loops. No GPU render of the faster solver was run for this entry. Timings measured on a quiet machine are in quiet_machine_timing_validation.

milestones.name: Multigrid-preconditioned pressure solve
milestones.validation: Conjugate-gradient projection preconditioned by one algebraic-aggregation V(1,1) cycle (2x2x2 aggregates, Galerkin operator, symmetric red-black Gauss-Seidel, coarse correction scaled by 1.5, dense Cholesky on at most 128 cells), with reductions over fixed 2048-cell blocks combined by a fixed binary tree. Tests: V-cycle symmetry and positivity with and without solids, exact Galerkin products, direct solve and mean removal on floating components, sealed fluid pockets (closed, open and expanding: an expanding pocket still fails with a pressure error because the removed mean stays in the final divergence check), equal results on 1, 2 and 8 threads with pinned hashes, iteration counts against resolution, and agreement with the Jacobi solver when both converge tightly. Measured on the impulse step at 128^3: Jacobi 275 iterations, multigrid 14.
milestones.limits: Convergence is judged by the RMS divergence over all fluid cells, so an error confined to a few cells of a large domain can pass. Multigrid results differ from Jacobi in the last bits, and the reference hashes hold only on x86_64 Linux. Iteration counts are not timings: no wall-time benefit is certified, and the solver has no visual review on the impact film.

milestones.name: MacCormack advection with an extrema limiter
milestones.validation: Backward-forward error correction (Selle et al., 2008) for density, temperature and the three velocity components, clamped to the minimum and maximum of the eight old values around the backward-trace origin and falling back to the semi-Lagrangian value where a collider cuts a trace. Free vortex (32^3 closed box, 60 force-free steps, multigrid): kinetic energy kept 96.6% against 68.8% and enstrophy 95.7% against 61.6% for semi-Lagrangian advection; the test requires 1.25x and 1.3x of the semi-Lagrangian values and energy that never grows. A swirling blob against a wall creates no new density or temperature extrema and leaves solid cells clean; results are equal on 1, 2 and 8 threads, with pinned hashes. The impact scene ran 144 steps at 64^3 and 128^3 without error.
milestones.limits: The advection stage measured 2.5x (64^3) and 2.4x (128^3) the semi-Lagrangian time on one thread, measured on a loaded machine and only on x86_64 Linux, not certified. Velocity uses the scheme on the strength of one vortex test; no visual comparison on the impact film was made. Hashes hold only on x86_64 Linux. Timings measured on a quiet machine are in quiet_machine_timing_validation.

milestones.name: Smoke memory estimate and resident state size
milestones.validation: The step memory estimate fell from 512 to 320 and then to 288 bytes per cell plus 8192, from a count of the live arrays (committed state 41, working state 41, solid-face list 56 if every cell were solid, pressure workspace 65, multigrid about 26), and a test pins the figure. Prescribed solid face velocities left the state, which now holds about 41 bytes per cell independent of colliders (a test checks 40-43 bytes per cell and that a step with a collider does not grow it); 30, 3 and 1 states fit 256 MiB at 64x52x64, 128x104x128 and 192x156x192 (14, 1 and none before). Reference hashes of both pressure solvers and both advection schemes pass unchanged. The least budgets the constructor accepts at those three resolutions were found by running it and are tabulated in the SREP. Peak resident memory on the impact scene (6 steps, multigrid, no colliders): 326 MB at 128x104x128 and 928 MB at 192x156x192.
milestones.limits: Peak resident memory depends on the allocator and on untouched pages, and was measured on a loaded machine and only on x86_64 Linux, not certified. milestones.name: Cheaper smoke volume export, cache key and checkpoints
milestones.validation: The five volume channels build in parallel and store whole 8x8x8 bricks (SparseGrid::set_brick, equivalent to 512 single sets and atomic on failure); the exported volume is identical to the previous implementation, compared bit for bit on five reference cases (colliders, odd and closed domains) and two temperature backgrounds. A volume is neither exported nor hashed when the simulation state did not change: four samples inside a fixed step return the same volume, a new step exports once, and a backward seek exports again and reproduces the first visit's key. The cache key hashes each brick on its own and combines the hashes in key order, so it is the same for any thread count; a flipped mantissa bit, swapped samples, another name or background, and 3000 single-voxel variations change it. Impact scene after 8 steps on a busy machine: export 610 to 77-100 ms at 128^3 and 2.2 s to 150-165 ms at 192^3; hashing 70 to 3 ms at 128^3 and 254 to 21 ms at 192^3; cloning a 192^3 state for a checkpoint took 102 ms.
milestones.limits: Timings were measured under load (load average about 12-14) on x86_64 Linux and are not certified. The key is an in-memory cache token whose values changed; no stored key and no test compares it with a fixed value. The dense velocity channels still dominate export time. Timings measured on a quiet machine are in quiet_machine_timing_validation.

milestones.name: Second-order ocean with a monotonized-central limiter
milestones.validation: Spec::order selects first order (default; a digest of the frame bits recorded from the earlier solver is unchanged for closed, open and periodic edges) or second order: MUSCL reconstruction of surface elevation and velocity with the monotonized-central limiter, depth-capped so face depths stay non-negative, first order at wet/dry fronts and non-periodic edge cells, SSP-RK2, a time-step bound halved to 0.225 and Strang-split drag. Amplitude lost by a 1e-3 wave after five wavelengths (order 1 / order 2): 99.96% / 77.2% at 10 cells per wavelength, 97.9% / 17.9% at 20, 85.3% / 2.6% at 40, 61.7% / 0.34% at 80. The minmod and van Leer limiters lost more at 10 and 20 cells (97.4% and 64.1%; 88.2% and 31.1%) and the choice rests on that comparison. Rest on rough bathymetry (to 1e-12), conservation on closed and periodic edges, positivity on wet/dry fronts over rough beaches, replay after checkpoint eviction and equality on 1, 2 and 8 threads pass in both orders.
milestones.limits: The bed-source term stays first order: second order holds for waves over a smooth bed. Non-negative depth at the 0.225 bound is verified by tests and not proven for the unsplit two-dimensional scheme; negative depth beyond round-off could not be provoked. Ten cells per wavelength still lose 77%, so waves need at least 20 cells per wavelength; the flux stays local Lax-Friedrichs. An absorbing edge (relaxation layer) was built and not adopted: for smooth pulses the zero-gradient open edge already reflects little (about 0% in one dimension, 3-7% against free space for a finite beam) and the layer reflected no less. Digests hold only on x86_64 Linux.

milestones.name: Ejecta thrown out by an impact: driver births in the 3D particle solver and burst@crater
milestones.validation: The 3D particle Driver can give, per fixed step window, births with exact instant, position, velocity and mass (mass kept in the particle); the 7 tests of particles3d_births cover birth at the exact instant, reverse replay and checkpoint budgets, ids and order among rate and burst births, no change for emitters that give none, an error and not a truncation above maxParticles with the published frame kept, windows asked once going forward, and births outside the window refused. milestones.name: Per-body water samples and owner tags in the ocean solver
milestones.validation: With Spec::body_owners the driver tags every occupied column with the body that holds most of it, and at each completed canonical step, next to Forcing::exchange, the driver is offered per body: the momentum that body gave the water in the step, the least-squares plane through the free surface of the wet columns of its footprint (level at the centre and two slopes), the depth-weighted mean horizontal water velocity, and the mean bed ordinate. The 7 tests of ocean_owners check that the per-body impulses add up to the total exchange to rounding, that a single body gave what all gave, bit-identical samples on replay with and without checkpoints (first and second order), that tagging does not change the water, an exact plane through a sloped surface (level, both slopes, velocity, bed) and no slope along a direction without extent, and the errors for an unknown tag and for tags without bodies; one evaluator test checks that two spheres and a crater surface in the colliders list tag their columns with their place in it. sr-sim, sr-model and sr-eval pass; clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.
milestones.limits: The solver delivers the samples; no consumer (reaction on the body, buoyancy from the perturbed surface) exists yet. A column held by several bodies is credited whole to the one with most of it. The tags cost 12 bytes per cell and 16 per body per checkpoint, charged only when body_owners is non-zero; the evaluator now sets it for every ocean that has body colliders, so those oceans are charged 12 bytes per cell more. Run time of the extra work (one owner pass and one footprint scan per canonical step) was measured on a 720x720 second-order ocean (the hero-hires grid) with a body of 1600 cells, 4 threads, on a machine at load 9 to 10, five alternating runs of 8 steps (examples/ocean_bodies_profile.rs): 1.130 s per step without tags and 1.203 s with them (about 6%), but the runs overlap (the last pair is inverted), so the cost is between nothing and about 10%, not resolved on this loaded machine. The hero-hires scene itself was not run for this entry.

milestones.name: Recent steps kept by the 3D particle emitter, for the samples of a motion-blur shutter
milestones.validation: A motion-blurred frame asks the evaluator for the frame and then for the shutter's samples (the first, the last, then each in turn), so the emitter is asked for a step ahead and then for steps behind it; each request that went back across a step restored the last checkpoint (up to a second of fixed steps earlier) and replayed from it. The emitter now also keeps its latest fixed steps (a quarter of checkpointMemoryMiB at most, none unless that holds three states, counted together with the checkpoints) and restarts from the latest stored state at or before the target, whichever kind. examples/blur_profile.rs asks a scene the way the renderer's sub-frame source does (40 frames from 2 s, 16 samples, 180 degree shutter, 20000 particles, step 1/120 s, a collider floor and a rigid ball): the 16 shutter samples cost 25.0 s of wall time per 40 frames before and 9.3 s after (the same scene with one sample: 1.1 to 2.0 s), and the combined hash of the particle frames was equal before and after, in the first scene (6000 particles, step 1/24 s, whose samples all lie inside one step, 2.8 s) as in this one. Tests (3, particles3d_recent): a sample that goes back replays no step with the recent steps against about 300 windows without them, frames equal to those of an emitter that keeps nothing, any scrubbing order agrees with a fresh emitter, and checkpoints plus recent steps stay within the budget for budgets from 1 KiB to 256 MiB.
milestones.limits: What remains is one partial step of every particle per distinct sample time (about 14 ms for 20000 particles on this loaded machine), which the exact frame at that instant needs; it grows with the number of samples. Measured on a loaded machine (load 8 to 14), only on this scene and on x86_64 Linux. No GPU render was run, and the sub-frame source of the renderer was imitated at the evaluator, not exercised.

milestones.name: Cavity of a body entering the water: waterImpulse@source and driver events in the ocean solver
milestones.validation: The solver takes impulses from the driver per canonical step (Forcing::events, those whose instant lies in (T - dt, T] at the sample that ends the step at T, validated and applied among the substeps in order of time after authored impulses of the same instant) and a Cavity impulse kind that moves the wanted volume or 90% of what its central disc holds, whichever is less, so it is limited by the water layer and never an error for lack of water. waterImpulse source=body (OCN10 to OCN12 in Schematron and Rust, 4 new corpus documents, oracle agreement with 279 documents) makes the cavity of the first entry of a dynamic body listed in colliders: the instant from the lowest point of its poses at the two ends of each step, the place under its centre, the volume and radius from the water row of the cratering law with its mass, its density (mass over the volume of its closed surface), its downward speed and the ocean's gravity. 7 solver tests (ocean_events): wanted volume moved from the disc to the ring with all the water kept, the limit and the failure of a negative displace in the same case, a dry or unresolved place does nothing, a driver-given impulse equal bit for bit to the authored one at the same instant (orders 1 and 2, three instants), nothing before the instant and identical replay with and without checkpoints, errors for an impulse outside its step or at the first sample, and a driver that asks for nothing changes nothing. 6 evaluator tests (water_entry): nothing before the entry and a change at it with a depression at the entry point, all the water kept, the far wave of the cavity alone (the difference with and without it) growing with speed (0.0033, 0.0071, 0.0170 for 10, 20, 30 m/s) and with mass (0.0024, 0.0071, 0.0207 for 500, 2000, 8000 kg), no cavity for a body that starts in the water, enters outside the ocean or moves away, shallow water neither an error nor an emptied column, and the same water after scrubbing and on a fresh evaluator. sr-sim, sr-model and sr-eval: 628 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored; clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.
milestones.limits: The combined far wave, with the body's own occupancy, is not monotone in speed in these runs (0.0326, 0.0390, 0.0276 at 10, 20, 30 m/s in 100 m of water): cavity and occupancy have opposite signs near the entry point and partly cancel, so the cavity alone does not give a wave that grows with the energy; the horizontal reaction on the body is not here. Only the first entry of a body makes a cavity; the cavity forms at once, not over the law's formation time, and is applied at the entry instant for the body's pose at the step ends; a disc smaller than four cells is widened with its volume kept. The law is that of a crater in water, not a validated model of water entry, and the model is hydrostatic with no jet or spray. The CLI and GPU were not run for this entry.

milestones.name: Ejecta of a growing crater land on its ground: births clear of the surface and a limit of their own for penetration recovery
milestones.validation: With the ground as the collider of burst@crater ejecta the 3D particle solver stopped with 'more than 16 collisions in one particle step' at 1.6 s of the land impact. Every one of those contacts was at fraction 0 (no time advanced): the impact point lies about 0.1 m inside the surface, so ejecta were born buried and pushed under the one-sided sheet (a particle then chased a floor sinking at 11 m/s), and a particle between two steep facets of the crater was pushed out of each in turn by a factor of about 0.3 per push, needing about 25 pushes to reach the contact tolerance. Ejecta of a crater are now born clear of the surface along the geometric normal of the owner by their largest collision radius plus the contact tolerance, and the solver counts contacts at fraction 0 apart from the 16 that move time forward, with a limit of 64 and its own error ('more than 64 penetration recoveries in one particle step'). milestones.name: Depth response of the ocean surface (bedResponse) and the form drag of bodies on the water
milestones.validation: ocean@bedResponse = depthFiltered (default) or hydrostatic (the first version, bit for bit). A displacement of the bed (crater) or of fluid (a body's thickness) is attenuated by the depth of the water: 1/cosh(kh) for the bed (Kajiura 1963, read only as quoted) and cosh(k z0)/cosh(kh) for a volume at height z0 above the bed (derived by the engine, equal to the former at z0 = 0 and to 1 at z0 = h), by a radix-2 FFT over a window of the footprint and four depths, one kernel per body, the displaced volume kept by renormalising what falls on wet columns of the domain. 6 solver tests (ocean_lift) against numerical integration of the same transforms: a sphere of 2 m radius on the bed of 20 m of water gives 0.02367 m at the centre against 0.02427 m by quadrature (2.5%), a volume at the surface is not attenuated (to 1e-9) and the filter falls monotonically with the height of the volume, a Gaussian of 10 m in 2 m of water keeps its shape and one of 2 m in 20 m matches the integral within 4%, totals kept with dry columns, edges and both signs, identical with 1, 2 and 8 threads, bad input an error. 8 evaluator tests (ocean_depth_filter): the instant the same sphere appears the surface rises 3.00 m hydrostatic and 0.026 m filtered (theory 0.024 m), 0.255 m and 0.017 m at 0.5 s; lifted volume 33.9 m3 for a sphere of 33.5 m3; a body at the surface is attenuated 0.54 against 0.0085 on the bed; a crater 40 m across in 6 m of water is within 5% of its hydrostatic trough and one 6 m across in 40 m of water 6.7 times smaller; no body in the water is bit-identical in both modes; a sphere of 2 m radius crossing 20 m of water at 10 m depth raises the highest surface 8.69 m (20 m/s) and 5.52 m (50 m/s) hydrostatic and 0.177 m and 0.198 m filtered; replay and 1, 2, 8 threads identical. In the filtered mode bodies give the water a push (Forcing::pushes, Spec::body_push): the form drag (1/2) C_d A |U - u| (U - u) per unit density, C_d = bodyDrag, A the wet frontal area from the body's own surface, applied evenly over the substeps column by column never past the body's velocity, with each body credited exactly what was applied: 6 solver tests (ocean_push: the water gains what is given, the cap, replay bit for bit with and without checkpoints, errors) and 4 evaluator tests (the first step of a sphere in still water is 104.05 against 104.72 for (1/2) C_d pi a^2 U^2 dt, the push falls as the water follows the body, the bodies' credits add up to the water's, frontal areas of a box, its cuts and a sphere within 1%). On the impact-ocean scene as first rendered (no cavity; 1.5 m cells, the scene and the code of that commit) the highest surface at 2.5 s goes from 10.62 m at (42.8, 0.8) to 0.16 m at (41.2, 0.8); with the cavity and bodyCoupling full from 9.92 m to 9.48 m. Cost per step on a 720 x 720 ocean at load 8 to 12: one body 0.140 and 0.138 s, ten bodies 0.141 and 0.162 s, a crater 0.123 and 0.128 s (hydrostatic and filtered); moving bodies 0.187 and 0.139 s, 0.176 and 0.179 s. sr-sim, sr-model, sr-eval: 724 passed, 0 failed, 9 ignored; clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.
milestones.limits: The filter is the response to an impulse; the propagation after it is that of shallow water, not dispersive; for a body in motion it is applied each canonical step, an approximation and not the solution for a moving source (not computed: only the stationary sphere is compared with theory, the moving ones are only shown to be far below the hydrostatic crest). The momentum kernel is that of the volume, a stand-in for the transfer function of a horizontal impulse, which was not derived. The form drag has one coefficient (default 1.0, an engine parameter; a real sphere is about 0.47), no added mass and no wake. The cavity of a water entry is not filtered, and is what remains of the crest on the impact-ocean scene with the cavity. A displacement wider than 1024 cells is not filtered. Kajiura (1963) was not read, only quoted literature; the generalisation to z0 is the engine's derivation. Timings under load, one machine. Tests that depend on the long-wave numbers of the first version set bedResponse=hydrostatic; OCN9 now says bodyDrag belongs to an ocean with colliders.
